turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hi.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hey.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hi. Can you hear me?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. I can hear you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Good. Um, my name is Doctor Gohil. I'm one of the physicians that works here at Babylon.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: May I confirm your name and date of birth, please?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, uh, my name is Sarah Smith. And, my date of birth is the twentieth of April nineteen eighty. Great.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Nineteen eighty three. And, are you in a space that's private and quiet, and you can talk?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Good. So, it says, erm, I've got a note to say, it says you're feeling short of breath. Is that correct?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Are you able to tell me a little bit more about that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. I was watching TV and, um, just like over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: That is, while you're sitting watching TV?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, have you noticed anything like this before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, apart from the shortness of breath, have you noticed anything else?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, so, I [inaudible] , I started with a cough yesterday.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um. Yeah. I, I don't know if it's, um, relevant, but I had a C-section a few weeks ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, how long ago was that? Just a few weeks?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, four weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, are you with baby at the moment?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I am.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, how is baby doing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. [inaudible] .

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any coughs or colds with, uh, them?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no. He's fine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So, you've noticed shortness of breath for just an hour, while sitting and watching TV?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yep. Mm-hmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, you had your C-section a couple of weeks ago?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, yesterday you noticed a cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, talk to me about the cough. Have you bought anything up?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I haven't, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, when was the last time you were ill with the flu, or symptoms like this?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, you know, I get coughs and colds quite a lot, but probably. Good few months ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, this shortness of breath you're having, is it getting worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um. No. I mean, I don't know. I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart, it's really going.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So, you're feeling your heart more than normal?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about when you take a very deep breath in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I mean, yeah. My chest feels sore, but so does my C-section scar. You know, it's, it's all tender.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, since your C-section, did you have to take any medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no. Just some painkillers.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: All right. And, can you remember what the name of those were?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, they gave me some, uh, Codeine.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, have you had to use that regularly?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah. I, I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly. But, probably haven't taken it for a week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, apart from the C-section and the shortness of breath, have you got any other medical problems I should know about?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. Um, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, you were [inaudible] .

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: [inaudible] tell you, I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, what happens when you take Ibuprofen?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um. I don't know. Sorry.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, I need you to do something for me. Have you measured the rate of your heart before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you measured it recently, either with an iWatch or something similar?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. We might need to do that over the phone. So, are you able to put your right hand on your left wrist, just underneath your thumb? And, see if you can feel your heartbeat.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yep. Yep.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, uh, what I need you to do is, when I count to three, count down from three, just [inaudible] count the number of beats you've noticed. And, I'll tell you when to stop. Is that OK?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm. Yep.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, we'll start in three, two, one. Go. Great. That should be enough. How many did you count?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I counted thirty.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Good. So, your heart is running slightly fast at the moment, which is probably because of the shortness of breath and some of the pain that you're under.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm. OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Given that you've had a C-section, and you're short of breath, which has come on quite recently and quite quickly It might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out the bit further.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, there's two ways of us doing this. The first is, I can call an ambulance. Or, you can take yourself to the hospital with baby.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Which one would you prefer?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, it feels a bit dramatic to call an ambulance. Um, I, I will, I will go. I will, I will take myself.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Sure. And, what I would suggest is, go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, if you're taking any medications like Codeine, don't, don't take them for the time being.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm, OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Is anyone else with you at home?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no. My partner's at work.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. So, I think that's the best thing to do, for the time being.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mm-hmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So, what I'm worried about at the moment is, given that you've had a C-section Some people can suffer with clots. And, those can either be found in the legs or your chest, so in your lungs.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: It's quite a common thing to happen. And, it's not something to worry about. But, needs to be checked out in the hospital first.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And, if it, if that does become the case, they can give you something to reduce the clot.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: All right, OK. That makes sense.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Fairly quick process.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK. Yeah. I mean, my mum's had, uh, clots in her legs before. So, I guess, you know. [inaudible] Yeah, that makes sense. I know, I know what they are.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Good. Are you, uh, are you particularly worried about anything, or do you want to ask me anything, before we go?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no. I'm fine. I'll, uh, I'll just take myself to the hospital.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Great. Thank you so much.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: All right. Thank you. Bye.
